_note: Rhythm/position rules JSON Schema cannot express. Each rule has severity error|warn and (where relevant) named exceptions. semantic_validate.py reads exceptions from THIS file (no second copy) and exports IMPLEMENTED_RULES; verify_all.py fails if a semantic rule here is not implemented or an implemented rule is missing here.

rules.description: At most one hero.marketing node per page. Templates that have no hero.marketing (install, manifesto, blog-index, blog-post, legal) are named exceptions to any 'hero required' reading: their H1 lives in install.intro / manifesto.opening / blog.intro / blog.article-header / legal.heading.

exceptions.note: verify_all.py checks this list equals the set of templates whose node list lacks hero.marketing

rules.description: A PageSpec's nodes must equal its declared template's node list: every required section present, in the template's order, with the template's fixed variant where one is set; extra or unknown sections are rejected.

shell.footer-closing is the last node on every template that has one, except that shell.floating-nav may follow it on home (Home.jsx renders <FloatingNav /> after <Footer />). The install template has no footer at all (named exception).
shell.floating-nav appears only on the home template (route /). Pricing, manifesto, blog, legal and install explicitly lack it.

Where a template uses the stand-alone shell.corner-nav it is the first node. Home and pricing embed the nav inside hero.marketing instead, and install has its own brand-only header (named exceptions).

The same (section, variant) pair must not appear in two adjacent nodes. A category-level adjacency rule is deliberately NOT used: the real pages legitimately run same-category sections back to back (four story.* sections on home, three pricing.* sections, five manifesto.* sections).
Sections with constraints.onePerPage appear once per page; sections with onePerPagePerVariant (manifesto.photo) appear once per (section, variant).
At most one node may use the scroll-pin-card-deck motion pattern per page (a single GSAP ScrollTrigger pin).
Every node carries motion.reducedMotionFallback equal to its section's locked fallback, and motion.patterns is a subset of the section's allowedPatterns.

measuredQuotes.contains: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: every animation has a reduced-motion branch

rules.description: Per (section, variant) required/forbidden content fields, forbidden motion patterns and pinned values from each section contract's variantRules (e.g. hero.marketing/home requires cta; hero.marketing/pricing forbids cta and the chroma sweep; shell.corner-nav/manifesto pins activeLink).

Every assetRef is reuse:<id> (id registered with the same role), generate:<brief> (only may-generate-new roles) or placeholder:neutral; the assetRole must be allowed for that field and pinned to its registry policy.
No string in a PageSpec may contain http:// or https:// (the clone makes no outbound requests); hrefs must be internal paths, anchors or mailto. The installer source is pinned to the local stub.
Every text field obeys its contract x-maxWords (and x-maxWordsTotal for lists), counted whitespace-separated, derived from recorded live word counts.
On the legal template legal.heading.activeTab must be 'privacy' for /privacy and 'terms' for /terms.
legal.heading.intro is present on /privacy and absent on /terms in the real pages; a /terms spec carrying an intro is warned about (not an error: a future legal page could add one).
The featured post's slug must not also appear in blog.story-list.stories (Blog.jsx destructures [featured, ...stories]); a spec that lists it twice reproduces the bug.
Exactly one plan card uses the primary (black) CTA variant (Ultra on the real page).
PageSpec.route must be a real route and be bound to PageSpec.template in templates/routes.json.
There is no monthly/annual billing toggle: pricing.plans content is closed, so any billing-toggle field is rejected by the schema.
